parsed_output.answer: Mendel’s monohybrid experiment involved crossing pea plants with contrasting traits to study how these traits are inherited. He selected pea plants because they have well-defined characters, are easy to cross-pollinate, and produce offspring in large numbers. In his experiment, Mendel crossed pure-bred pea plants with yellow seeds (YY) and pure-bred pea plants with green seeds (yy). All the offspring in the first generation (F1) had yellow seeds, indicating that the yellow seed trait is dominant. When these F1 plants were self-pollinated, the second generation (F2) showed a 3:1 ratio of yellow to green seeds. This demonstrated the Law of Dominance, which states that in a pair of alleles, the dominant trait is expressed in the presence of the recessive trait. The experiment also showed that traits are inherited independently, and each parent contributes one allele to the offspring.
